detail.longDescription: I have been developing software using manual version control; before any significant change, I made copies of files to be changed and renamed them to names suggesting what was changed, plus keeping description of changes in additional text file. This is basically a manual equivalent of git commits. This worked well, but now I'm switching to git, mostly to use it as a tool to quickly deploy my applications to other servers, without having to manually copy all the files (and remembering everything that is there to be copied). One thing that I find very annoying is that git does not store timestamps of the committed files in the commits, and because of this when you do git clone or git pull , it sets timestamps of new/modified files to current time, not to the time when the file was originally modified before it was committed to the repo. The file timestamp is a very important factor to me to get a quick view of what was modified when. For example I cannot quickly, just by looking at the directory, check whether the files on two servers are the same or not. It makes the function "Compare directories" in Midnight Commander, which I use a lot, non-functional. is there any method (maybe via some addon or plugin) to make git remember timestamps of committed files and restoring them when fetching files from the repository?
